rows.notes: The cited document is a literature review (title and Section 2 'Review methodology' describe a database search and summary of papers from 2009-2019). It reports no own data, experiment, survey or validated model runs; Fig. 6 only illustrates an IoT monitoring setup without reporting results. Q1 is 'no', so Q2-Q9 are 'no'. The review does discuss closed-loop/MPC control as routes to water use efficiency and robustness under uncertainty, but only by citing other work.

Review article, not a primary study (Q1 'no'). The claim that feedback control prevents persistent over/under-irrigation under weather or soil uncertainty is discussed in Sections 5.1-5.2 (open- vs closed-loop) only via cited sources (e.g., Montesano et al. 2016 timer vs sensor-based leaching), not from the authors' own results.

Review article with no own empirical result (Q1 'no'). Statements about improved timing/amount decisions reducing over-application are synthesised from cited literature; no own measurement of excess irrigation reduction.

Review article (Q1 'no'). The review frames benefits as water use efficiency/water saving throughout, but does not itself report or analyse any rebound or reallocation of saved water to expanded irrigated area; the passage's nuance is not found in this document.

Review article (Q1 'no'). The review mentions, as general discussion, sensor calibration/installation challenges, dependence of ANN/fuzzy accuracy on data quality and expert knowledge, and sprinkler/drip maintenance issues, but does not report own findings on sensor drift, communication dropouts or coverage degrading automated irrigation performance.

Review article (Q1 'no'). The authors argue that advanced control (MPC, fuzzy, ANN) depends on accurate models, quality sensor data and expert rules, and cite water-saving results (e.g., 40% from Lefkowitz 2019, 52% from Tseng et al. 2018), but all are cited, not own results.

Review article (Q1 'no'). No own evidence on risk management (e.g., avoiding water stress or yield loss) from advanced control; discussion of robustness to disturbances and uncertainty (MPC, PID windup) is drawn from cited studies.

notes: Abioye et al. (2020) is a narrative literature review of monitoring and advanced control strategies for precision irrigation (Section 2 describes database search and paper selection; Figs. 1-3 are bibliometric counts). It contains no primary experiment, survey or validated model; Fig. 6 shows a monitoring setup at UTM orchard but no results are reported. All seven rows therefore receive 'no' on Q1 and consequently on Q2-Q9. Text appears complete (pages 1-22 including references).
